summary.text: A woman aged 27 years presented in February 2023 with primary infertility, prolonged menstruation and worsening lower abdominal pain (VAS 9) and a painful nodular posterior vaginal fornix mass. Serum CA125 was reported as elevated at 67.88 U/mL, with no date in the text, and she was diagnosed with deep infiltrating endometriosis. Further examination found vaginal fornix nodules, a fixed left adnexa, a hard pelvic floor mass and colonoscopic chronic inflammation findings.

The multidisciplinary team recommended prompt surgery; because infertility was the main concern, IVF with oocyte retrieval was done first in July 2023 (six blastocysts cryopreserved), followed by three GnRH-a doses. A 7-h laparoscopic surgery with partial rectal and vaginal resection and colorectal anastomosis followed in November 2023, with one postoperative GnRH-a dose.

Follow-up showed improved pelvic mobility and a VAS pain score reduced from 9 to 1; CA125 declined after surgery. In March 2024 a natural cycle embryo transfer gave a pregnancy, and a live male infant with Apgar 10 at 1 and 5 min was delivered by cesarean section at 38 weeks and 5 days.

summary.text: A woman aged 31 years with a 3-year history of primary infertility and a 2018 right salpingo-oophorectomy for an ovarian serous cystadenoma presented in August 2021 with an abnormal posterior fornix, CA125 22.75 U/mL and uterine fibroids. Primary intestinal disorders were ruled out.

After an IVF cycle in November 2021 (three blastocysts cryopreserved), two artificial-cycle frozen embryo transfers failed. In April 2023 menstrual pain scored 10 on the VAS with narrowing of stool; imaging showed left hydroureteronephrosis from distal ureteral stenosis, and DIE was diagnosed. A repeat IVF in May 2023 yielded two blastocysts.

In July 2023 she had an 11-h extensive laparoscopic procedure, followed by oral dienogest for 4 months. By October 2023 CA125 had fallen to 18.7 U/mL and follow-up imaging confirmed resolution of hydronephrosis; bowel function normalized and pain fell to 2 on the VAS. A natural cycle embryo transfer in March 2024 led to a pregnancy, and a healthy male infant with Apgar 10 at 1 and 5 min was delivered by cesarean section at 35 weeks and 1 day for fetal growth restriction secondary to pregnancy-induced hypertension.
